name: INA293A4IDBVR
title: -4 V to 110 V common-mode, 1.3 MHz, fixed-gain unidirectional current-sense amplifier
summary: INA293 senses the voltage across a shunt whose common-mode voltage may sit anywhere from -4 V to +110 V, independent of its own 2.7 V to 20 V supply, and drives a ground-referred output equal to the shunt voltage times a fixed gain of 20, 50, 100, 200 or 500 V/V. A zero-drift input and a transconductance stage built round a current-feedback amplifier give ±0.15% maximum gain error, 160 dB typical DC CMRR and up to 1.3 MHz bandwidth. It measures one direction of current only. INA293A4IDBVR is the gain-200, pinout-A part in a 5-pin SOT-23 on a 3000-piece reel.

circuits.title: Unidirectional high-side sensing from a 48 V supply
circuits.description: A shunt sits between a 48 V supply and the load, whose other end goes to ground. IN+ takes the supply end of the shunt and IN- the load end, so supply-to-load current produces a positive VSENSE. The amplifier runs from 5 V and OUT carries VSENSE times the gain, referred to GND.

circuits.title: Differential RC filter at the input pins
circuits.description: The shunt runs from the common-mode source VCM to the load. Each end of the shunt reaches its input pin through its own series resistor RIN, and CIN joins IN+ and IN- after the resistors, forming a differential low-pass filter. RIN should be 10 Ω or less; the gain error factor equations give the added error.

circuits.title: Solenoid current sensing at a half-bridge output
circuits.description: Two N-channel MOSFETs form a half bridge on a 24 V rail, both gates driven by a microcontroller. A 50 mΩ shunt runs from the bridge output to the solenoid (an inductance with its winding resistance) whose far end is grounded. The gain-50 amplifier, powered from 5 V, reads the shunt with IN+ on the bridge side and feeds OUT to the microcontroller's ADC. The common-mode voltage swings from 0 V to 24 V with the bridge, and the maximum current is 1.5 A.

operation.text: Five gains are offered, each in two SOT-23 pinouts; the digit after A or B picks the gain (1 = 20, 2 = 50, 3 = 100, 4 = 200, 5 = 500, in V/V). In the tables x stands for either pinout (INA293x4 covers A4 and B4). An AEC-Q100 automotive version is sold as INA293-Q1.

The amplifier is a transconductance stage built round a current-feedback amplifier, which holds input bias current near 20 µA even at 110 V common mode, with a zero-drift input. The gain is set by internal input resistors R1 and an output resistor RL (fixed gain resistor table).

The inputs work from -4 V to +110 V whatever the supply voltage, so the same part serves high-side and low-side shunts. Going below ground lets it follow recirculating current in half-bridge stages. The inputs survive -20 V to +120 V.

Small-signal bandwidth falls as gain rises (1.3 MHz at 20 V/V, 900 kHz at 200 and 500 V/V) and also depends on VSENSE: bandwidth is highest at larger sense voltages, rising with output voltage until it levels off. Acceptable high-frequency error has to be judged in the end circuit.
Each input draws about 20 µA at common-mode voltages up to 110 V. With a differential input present, the internal bias network makes IB+ and IB- differ, growing with VSENSE.
The zero-drift input keeps offset and drift low across -40 °C to +125 °C, so small sense voltages from low-value shunts can be read accurately, cutting shunt loss.

Gain comes from an internal resistor network whose ratios match closely though each resistor's own value can differ a lot; for that reason adding external resistance to alter the gain is not recommended. Gain error is under 0.15% at room temperature and drifts at most 10 ppm/°C from -40 °C to +125 °C. Choose the gain for the needed signal-to-noise ratio.

The part runs from 2.7 V to 20 V. At 20 V supply the gain-20 version accepts up to 1 V differential input. The output can only swing within the supply on VS, while the inputs may sit far outside it: a 5 V supply serves inputs anywhere in the -4 V to 110 V span.

Only current flowing from the supply into the load is measured. With zero input the output sits at most 20 mV above GND, so keep the differential input at or above 20 mV divided by the gain to stay in the linear range.

With 1.3 MHz bandwidth at 20 V/V and 2.5 V/µs slew rate the part suits fast inrush and overcurrent detection: with gain 20, a 2 mΩ shunt and a 75 A trip point, the output climbs to its 3 V trip level in under 2 µs.

A larger shunt raises the signal and shrinks the share of offset error, but its size and dissipation set an upper limit. Both output swing limits must also be checked: full-scale current times shunt times gain must stay below the positive swing, and minimum current times shunt times gain must stay above the negative swing. If the shunt chosen for dissipation is too big for the positive swing, a lower gain fixes it. Higher-gain versions allow smaller shunts with less dissipation (10 A, 5 V full scale: 25 mΩ and 2.5 W at gain 20, 1 mΩ and 0.1 W at gain 500).

Filtering is not needed for accurate results and an input filter is not recommended. A filter at the output works but raises the impedance seen by the next stage. If an input filter is used, keep each series resistor at 10 Ω or less: the unequal bias currents of the two inputs flow through the filter resistors and add a differential error, and resistor tolerance mismatch adds to it. The gain error factor equations give the effect; 10 Ω resistors cost -0.29% at gain 20 up to -0.74% at gain 500.
A negative differential input drives the part into overload, and recovery takes time after VSENSE is positive again. The more negative the input was, the longer the recovery.
Fit a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor right at the VS and GND pins, nearer being better. A supply that is noisy or has high source impedance may take extra decoupling.

Connect the inputs to the shunt with a Kelvin (four-wire) connection so that only the shunt resistance lies between IN+ and IN-. Because the shunt value is so small, any high-current trace resistance between the inputs adds large error. The recommended layout puts the bypass capacitor next to VS with a via to the ground plane at GND.
